identity.real_world_identity_notes: Aston Martin documents the Vantage GT4 Evo with a production-derived eight-speed transmission configured to use six forward ratios. AMS2 presents those six usable ratios through steering-wheel paddles.

wheel_rim.notes: Direct AMS2 cockpit inspection matched the Aston Martin racing wheel reference: an open-top GT rim without an integrated display. Exact diameter remains unknown.

notes: With Auto Clutch disabled, the car moved from rest without physical clutch input. The underlying simulator mechanism was not established.
All six usable paddle-selected forward gears accepted clutch-free full-throttle upshifts without driver lift, with automatic cut perceptible.
Clutch-free downshifts were accepted with no driver throttle input, and automatic blip was directly visible as a throttle-display spike.

The normalized sequential-paddle description represents the driver's six-ratio control interface in AMS2; the official source describes the underlying real transmission as a production-derived eight-speed unit configured to use six ratios.
Live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with Auto Clutch disabled.
Clutch-free move-off, six no-lift paddle upshifts with automatic cut, clutch-free downshifts with automatic blip, and the open-top no-display rim were directly observed.
The mechanism permitting clutch-free move-off was not determined.

confidence.basis: The exact identity and complete user-facing six-ratio paddle control technique were directly checked in AMS2; Aston Martin independently documents the production-derived transmission and six usable forward ratios.

claims.basis: Official release and manufacturer material agree with the exact live model and class identity observed through SimHub 9.11.22.
Aston Martin documents the production-derived eight-speed transmission as using six forward ratios, and all six were directly exercised through the paddles in AMS2.
Sequential is the normalized project category for the simulated driver's ordered paddle interface; the record explicitly preserves the underlying production-derived eight-speed hardware description.

Direct testing established clutch-free move-off, clutch-free no-lift upshifts with perceptible cut, and clutch-free downshifts with a visible automatic-blip spike. The move-off mechanism remains explicitly unknown.
Direct cockpit inspection and the supplied Aston Martin wheel reference classified the open-top no-display rim as GT-style in the project vocabulary.

notes: The difference between the real production-derived gearbox hardware and the normalized simulated paddle interface is intentionally retained.

The wheel-rim shape was originally recorded as "gt-style". The separate "gt-style", "formula" and "prototype" values described the same rim: molded grips at 9 and 3 with a control face between them, usually carrying a display and rev lights. They are merged into "gt-formula". The rim was not observed again and nothing about the observation changed.
